Repo: /home/mudathir/all/cvc5/mudathir (cvc5 SMT solver, branch lazy).
Goal: in src/theory/arith/liastar/liastar_extension.cpp, replace the per-lambda incremental
subsolver with enumeration in the MAIN solver: fresh integer skolems y for the lambda's bound
variables, a boolean guard skolem h (decision variable, phase-preferred true), lemmas
h => base(y) and h => not(D_i(y)) sent via TheoryArith's InferenceManager, the next cell read
from the main solver's candidate arithmetic model, and completeness detected when h is forced
false at decision level 0. Answer the specific questions for your assigned area with exact
signatures and file:line references. Return raw facts, not prose essays.
Area: src/theory/valuation.h (+ .cpp). Questions:
1. Exact signatures of: ensureLiteral, isSatLiteral, hasSatValue, isDecision, getDecisionLevel,
   and ANY method that tells whether a literal is FIXED/entailed at decision level 0 (isFixed?).
   For getDecisionLevel: what does it return for unassigned literals / non-SAT literals? Safe call order?
2. Is there a getModelValue / getCandidateModelValue on Valuation usable at LAST_CALL effort from a
   theory extension? Signature and constraints.
3. How does the existing liastar code use Valuation (search liastar_extension.cpp for getValuation)?

   * @param texp The explained propagation.

  void notifyExplainedPropagation(TrustNode texp);

  /**
   * Configure the preferred phase of a decision variable. This occurs
   * *globally*, i.e., even if the literal is untranslated by user pop and
   * retranslated, it keeps this phase.
   *
   * @note This phase is always enforced when the SAT solver decides to make a
   *       decision on this variable on its own. If a decision is injected into
   *       the SAT solver via TheoryProxy::getNextDecisionRequest(), the
   *       preferred phase will only be considered if the decision was derived
   *       by the decision engine. It will be ignored if the decision was
   *       derived from a theory (the phase enforced by the theory overrides
   *       the preferred phase).
   *
   * @param n the node in question; must have an associated SAT literal
   * @param phase the phase to use
   */
  void preferPhase(TNode n, bool phase);

  /**
   * Return whether the given literal is a SAT decision.  Either phase
   * is permitted; that is, if "lit" is a SAT decision, this function
   * returns true for both lit and the negation of lit.
   */
  bool isDecision(Node lit) const;

  /**
   * Get the current list of decisions made by the SAT solver at the moment in
   * time that getPropDecisions() is called.
   *
   * @return List of decisions made by the SAT solver.
   */
  std::vector<Node> getPropDecisions() const;

  /**
   * Get the order heap from the SAT solver.
   * order_heap is a priority queue of variables ordered with
   * respect to the variable activity. The order heap is made available here
   * in order to make partitions based on the literals contained in the heap.
   *
   * @return List of Nodes from the SAT variables order heap.
   */
  std::vector<Node> getPropOrderHeap() const;

  /**
   * Return whether lit has a fixed SAT assignment (i.e., implied by input
   * assertions).
   */
  bool isFixed(TNode lit) const;

  /**
   * Checks the current context for satisfiability.
   *
   */
  Result checkSat();

   * Get the value of a boolean variable.
   *
   * @return mkConst<true>, mkConst<false>, or Node::null() if
   * unassigned.
   */
  Node getValue(TNode node) const;

content.text: All questions answered from the source. Compiling the facts.

facts: Q1 ensureLiteral: `CVC5_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT Node ensureLiteral(TNode n);` at src/theory/valuation.h:158; impl src/theory/valuation.cpp:177-181 delegates to PropEngine::ensureLiteral. Doc (valuation.h:146-157): may add lemmas to the SAT solver; the returned node may DIFFER from the input due to theory-rewriting/preprocessing/CNF conversion, and only the returned node is queryable via getSatValue. Always store and use the returned node.

Q1 isSatLiteral: `bool isSatLiteral(TNode n) const;` at src/theory/valuation.h:75; impl valuation.cpp:76-80 -> PropEngine::isSatLiteral = d_cnfStream->hasLiteral(node) (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:568-571). Safe on any node.

Q1 hasSatValue: two overloads: `bool hasSatValue(TNode n, bool& value) const;` (valuation.h:98) and `bool hasSatValue(TNode n) const;` (valuation.h:102). Impl valuation.cpp:104-114 -> TheoryEngine::hasSatValue (src/theory/theory_engine.cpp:843-861), which FIRST checks d_propEngine->isSatLiteral(n) and returns false for non-SAT literals, so it is safe to call without guarding. Returns false (value unmodified) if literal is unassigned (SAT_VALUE_UNKNOWN, see PropEngine::hasValue prop_engine.cpp:573-596, which itself Asserts hasLiteral but TheoryEngine guards that).

Q1 getSatValue (related): `Node getSatValue(TNode n) const;` valuation.h:85; returns Node::null() if no current assignment, else true/false constant; handles a NOT wrapper explicitly (valuation.cpp:82-101). Underlying PropEngine::getValue Asserts d_cnfStream->hasLiteral(node) (prop_engine.cpp:545-548), so guard with isSatLiteral first.

Q1 isDecision: `bool isDecision(Node lit) const;` at src/theory/valuation.h:189; impl valuation.cpp:197-201 -> PropEngine::isDecision (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:384-388) which does `Assert(isSatLiteral(lit))` then queries the SAT solver; NOT safe on non-SAT literals. Phase-insensitive (true for lit and its negation, valuation.h:183-188). Minisat semantics (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.h:640-646): `vardata[x].d_reason == CRef_Undef && level(x) > 0`, i.e. true only for variables currently assigned by a decision at level > 0.

Q1 getDecisionLevel: DOES NOT EXIST in this codebase. grep for getDecisionLevel/decisionLevel over all of src/ (valuation, prop_engine, sat_solver interface) finds nothing exposed; Minisat's internal `int level(Var)` (src/prop/minisat/core/Solver.h:648) is not surfaced through SatSolver/PropEngine/Valuation. The closest public APIs are isFixed (below) and `unsigned getAssertionLevel() const;` (valuation.h:200, impl valuation.cpp:209-212 -> PropEngine::getAssertionLevel prop_engine.cpp:689-692) which is the USER push/pop level, not the SAT decision level.

Q1 isFixed (the level-0/entailed test): `bool isFixed(TNode lit) const;` at src/theory/valuation.h:195, doc: 'Return whether lit has a fixed SAT assignment (i.e., implied by input assertions)'. Impl valuation.cpp:203-207 -> PropEngine::isFixed (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:406-413) which returns false for non-SAT literals (internally guarded, safe to call on anything). MinisatSatSolver::isFixed (src/prop/minisat/minisat.cpp:291-295): `intro_level(var)==0 && user_level(var)==0 && level(var)==0`, i.e. variable assigned at SAT decision level 0 AND introduced/asserted at user assertion level 0. It is phase-insensitive: to detect 'h forced false at level 0' use `bool val; valuation.hasSatValue(h, val) && !val && valuation.isFixed(h)`.

Q1 safe call order: (1) h = valuation.ensureLiteral(h) once at creation, keep the returned node; (2) hasSatValue and isFixed may be called unguarded; (3) getSatValue and isDecision must be guarded by isSatLiteral. For unassigned literals: getSatValue returns Node::null(), hasSatValue returns false, isFixed returns false, isDecision returns false (reason undef but level(x)>0 fails only if level array is stale; in practice unassigned vars are not decisions).

Q2 getCandidateModelValue: `Node getCandidateModelValue(TNode var);` at src/theory/valuation.h:115 (doc valuation.h:110-114: candidate model value computed at full effort, prior to theory combination and final model construction; null if not available). Impl valuation.cpp:122-126 -> TheoryEngine::getCandidateModelValue (src/theory/theory_engine.cpp:1372-1382): returns var if var.isConst(); otherwise `Assert(d_sharedSolver->isShared(var))` -- only legal for SHARED terms -- then delegates to the type-owning theory's Theory::getCandidateModelValue (default returns Node::null(), src/theory/theory.h:443-446). TheoryArith override: src/theory/arith/theory_arith.h:119, src/theory/arith/theory_arith.cpp:511-519 (strips TO_REAL, checks d_arithModelCache, falls back to d_internal.getCandidateModelValue).
